title: Life Is a Paradox
summary: A reflection on duality, detachment, and the practice of observing life without being kicked around by every moment.

blocks.text: Life is a **paradox**. Whatever you see around yourself is never singular. Stop wanting things to be singular and streamlined.

Rather than being the soccer player on the field, for a moment be the **observer** who stands behind the line and watches how the game is fashioned. Rather than looking at life only by immersing in it, detach from it for a while, step out, and look around at people, things, and objects. You start realizing many underlying truths of this world.

blocks.alt: Misty mountains and rice terraces under sunlight.

blocks.text: People love diamonds, don't they? Diamonds are found with coal. The world's most expensive jewelry is found in dirt. Oxygen, the vital source of life for all organisms on Earth, is never in the air in its purest form. It exists with nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and many other gases that compose the air.

No element in the periodic table was simply found in its purest form lying around; it was discovered through extensive research. Humans worship God and spread messages of meditation and calmness, but also sin, get angry, and make mistakes. Wars are fought to attain peace. This world is a juxtaposition, a paradox. Nothing exists only singularly; the basis of this world is dual.
The Frustration of Wanting Only One Side

We all strive to live life singularly. In what sense? We only want happy things to happen. We go on a vacation and want everything to fall perfectly. After a tiring day at work, we want the restaurant to serve perfect, delicious food. And if they don't, we crash out and say, "After all this tiring day, I wanted one small retreat, and I couldn't get it."

We just can't accept that this world's fundamental nature is **duality**. Nothing can exist only in its purest form. Happiness doesn't magically arrive and stay forever. Happiness comes with sadness, and sadness comes with happiness. Life is a mixture of moments.

Most people stay upset because they cannot accept this foundation. They say, "Whenever a good thing happens to me, I'm scared grief will follow." If there is day, there is night. If there is summer, there is winter. For spring, there is fall.
Observe Instead of Clinging

Life is a journey of moments. Based on impact, we call them positive or negative. But what if you stop judging, stop assuming you are just another object in the game, and instead experience things and let them pass?

Suppose you visit your dream country with your special person and enjoy life fully. You don't want it to end. You affirm, "I just want to stay here, I don't want to go back." Instead of gripping that feeling, experience and observe how happiness moves through your senses and mind, makes you feel lighter, and then let it pass with a smile on the flight back.

Then when you return to professional life and your boss says something that hurts you, instead of saying, "Last week was perfect and now I'm in a mess," accept that life's nature is dual. It gives experiences. If you immerse in every moment, judge each one, and let emotion take charge, you end up saying, "I am depressed this week."

blocks.alt: Observe it, don't absorb it illustration.

blocks.text: You are here to observe how moments pass by. If you make every harsh word your own identity, sadness and heaviness follow. Stop classifying moments as good and bad; look at them as moments. They come and go, and you witness how they touch your emotions.
Be the Observer, Not the Ball

Start being that soccer **observer** who sees every player (every moment), the ball (the body), and the audience (the emotions) clearly. If you become only a player chasing the ball everywhere, what difference remains between you and the ball? Both are kicked around by moments.
Realize you are not reactive to moments or to the audience. You can be active, independent, and aware. Experience joy, sadness, jealousy, anger, and temptation, and let them pass.

When your boss scolds you for petty things, smile inwardly and remember: "I am observing the game. The boss is a player, my feelings are the audience, and I am the observer." You are not the ball getting kicked around in this field of life.

pairs.hidden: Notice the joy fully, then name one way to return home without clinging to the high.

pairs.prompt: Moment 2: A harsh comment at work.
pairs.hidden: Pause before reacting; describe the event as if you were a neutral observer.

blocks.text: Some people ask: if I detach from my boss's cruel words, won't I lose the drive to grow and switch jobs?
One answer: your boss's treatment should not be the core motivational factor for changing jobs. You should change because you see a place where you can grow and achieve faster.

Second answer: detachment gives a 3D perspective. When you play the game, you only see the ball and your feet. As a spectator, you see the field, other players, uneven grass, formations, and all factors shaping the game.

Attachment to your activity ties your whole identity to something as temporary as shifting sand. Try to draw your positivity from that ground, and it will not be long before it changes shape and brings you negativity instead. Tie yourself to shifting sand, and your inner state keeps getting **pulled** around without end.
The singular feeling of joy appears when you stop treating yourself as the soccer ball that gets kicked around, and begin standing as the observer of the game.

Happiness is your own state; peace is your own property. Just as a circle's defining quality is roundness, peace is native to your nature. If it is not round, it cannot be a circle; in the same way, your deepest self—your soul—is peace.
If you attach your identity to temporary outer activity, whether good or bad, your independence slips into unstable things that keep changing form.

blocks.alt: A meditative Buddha painting in warm tones.

blocks.text: The art of detachment cannot be learned by reading alone. It must be practiced.

tabs.content:

I am this moment. If this fails, I fail.

tabs.label: Detached lens
tabs.content:
![Detached lens meditation image](/images/life-is-a-paradox/lens-detached.png)
I am aware of this moment. I can respond without becoming it.

tabs.label: Integrated lens
tabs.content:
![Integrated lens meditation image](/images/life-is-a-paradox/lens-integrated.png)
I feel fully, act clearly, and release what has passed.

blocks.text: Practice turns detachment from concept into lived skill. Use this order when emotion rises.

blocks.text: Move through this reminder when your mind swings between extremes.

slides.title: Peak
slides.body: Enjoy deeply, but do not demand permanence.

slides.title: Dip
slides.body: Feel fully, but do not build identity around pain.

slides.title: Flow
slides.body: Return to observer mode: this is a moment, not the whole of you.
